newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday December 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday December 23.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The parliament approved the centre-left government's 1997 austerity budget, which aims to slice 62.5 trillion lire from next year deficit. The centre-right Freedom Alliance and the secessionist Northern League party boycotted the vote to protest against the bill (all).

* In a letter to a newspaper, leftist PDS party leader Massimo D'Alema defends his strategy of a dialogue with opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi to carry out constitutional reforms. The PDS is the largest party in the centre-left government coalition (Repubblica).
* In an interview, Berlusconi reaffirms the need for a broad political coalition: "It is a serious solution to a serious crisis" (Il Messaggero).

* Italian Renewal, a small centrist party which backs the government and is headed by Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, has split up in parliament after months of infighting: 11 deputies may decide to break away leaving Dini's with just 14 members in the lower house (all).

* Metalworkers unions welcome a compromise deal put forward by the government, but employers association Federmeccanica says "It will be very difficult to accept the government's proposal" which includes a pay rise of 200,000 lire (all).

* The Treasury will issue on January 2 a new tranche of three and five years BTP fixed rate bonds with lower coupons: 6.0 percent down from 7.50 percent for the 3-year BTPs, and 6.25 percent down from 7.75 percent for the 5-year bond (Il Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
